vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-85091
vulnerability.description: zlib gz_vacate() heap buffer overflow: a non-blocking gzwrite() that stalls leaves a stale external buffer pointer, and a later gzprintf() or gzvprintf() moves more bytes than the internal input buffer holds.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw sits in zlib's gz* file writing API (gzwrite, gzprintf, gzvprintf) and needs a gz stream opened for writing on a non-blocking descriptor that stalls. Nothing in this image writes gzip files through that API: git links only the deflate and inflate stream entry points for its objects and packs, git-lfs is a Go binary with its own compress/flate, and Bun's zlib bindings expose stream compression only. The application itself never opens gz streams. Debian ships zlib 1:1.3.dfsg+really1.3.1-1 in trixie and has no fix in any release (bug #1146895); upstream describes the affected range as 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2.
